title: JURY MANAGEMENT SOLUTION (JMS) SYSTEM

input.agency: ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICE OF THE US COURTS
input.description_text: ALSO KNOW AS THE JURY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (JMS). This is a pre-solicitation notice for a web-based Jury Management System (JMS) solution and is prepared in accordance with Judiciary Guide Volume 14, § 330 Standard Competitive Contracting Procedures as supplemented with additional information included in this notice, for the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AO). This solicitation is unrestricted and is not set aside for small business. The Judiciary is not subject to the FAR to include small business regulations. The AO is seeking to award a single award Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract for a commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS), web-based Jury Management Solution (JMS) to assist the courts with the selection, management, and tracking of jurors, as well as performing financial and statistical calculations including interfacing with the Judiciary’s financial management system, Momentum. The attached DRAFT solicitation USCA27R0009 provides details on the requirement, instructions, and evaluation criteria. Responsible sources shall follow the instructions in the attached RFP. Responses to this solicitation are due no later than 3:00 P.M. ET on TBD, 2026, late submissions may not be accepted. Offers must be emailed in accordance with instructions in Section L-0 of the RFP. NO QUESTIONS WILL BE ACCEPTED FOR THE PRE-SOLICITATION. No phone calls will be accepted. title: PRIMED-AI: Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnerships (D2M-AIP) for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (UG3/UH3 Clinical Trial Optional)

input.description_text: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is to catalyze the development and testing of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled, image-centered, multimodal Clinical Decision Support (CDS) tools, developed in pursuance as Software as a Medical Device (SaMD). These projects are expected to have high potential for demonstrable, positive impact on patient outcomes and/or healthcare processes.

title: Defense Health Agency (DHA), Program Acquisition Executive, Digital Medical Solutions (PAE DMS), Enterprise Intelligence & Data Solutions (EIDS) Program Management Office (PMO), Data Exchange Services Operations, Modernization, and Development

input.description_text: Area of Interest (AOI) #02: Data Exchange Services Operations, Modernization, and Development PAE DMS is interested in solutions that satisfy the Government’s need for Data Exchange Services operations, modernization, and development in support of the Enterprise Information and Data Solutions (EIDS) Program Management Office (PMO). This AOI #02 is published under the authority of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), HT003826SC005, available at: https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/cd16b90540b7407fb4de1e028cea74d4/view Consistent with the maturity and nature of the selected commercial solution and applicable law, the Government may use any applicable award authority identified in the CSO. The DHA Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Defense Medical Solutions (PAE DMS), EIDS PMO, seeks commercial solutions to support Data Exchange Platform (DxP) operations, sustainment, modernization, and development. The DxP supports mission-essential MHS Information Platform (MIP) functions by processing real-time clinical and operational data exchanged with more than 15 external systems and partners. It enables secure, standards-based interoperability among DHA, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and other Federal healthcare partners in support of military health readiness and patient-care delivery. The Government seeks commercial solutions that sustain reliable, secure, and continuously available legacy services while modernizing the platform toward scalable, cloud-native, API-driven, standards-based, and AI/ML-ready capabilities. Solutions may be commercially available or capable of configuration, integration, testing, demonstration, or modification to meet Government objectives. Responses will inform the Government’s assessment of solution maturity, technical feasibility, commercial viability, and potential acquisition pathways. Proprietary Information and Non-Government Advisors Respondents may submit proprietary information. Respondents are responsible for adequately marking all proprietary, restricted, or competition-sensitive information contained in their submissions. Marked information will be protected from disclosure outside Government personnel unless the respondent grants permission for Government support contractors to review the material. The following companies and individual employees are contractually bound by Organizational Conflict of Interest and disclosure clauses regarding proprietary information. They will take all reasonable action necessary to preclude unauthorized use or disclosure of respondent proprietary data: Boston Consulting Group (BCG) Andrew Morgan, LLC Submission under this AOI constitutes the submitting company’s authorization for the Government to use non-Government advisors during all phases of the AOI review. Companies with concerns regarding support-contractor access to proprietary information should contact the points of contact (POCs) before submission. Submission Method and Due Dates Vendors must submit Phase I responses electronically to Lacey Lockard at lacey.n.lockard.civ@health.mil no later than 28 October 2026, 1400 Eastern Time. The Government will not consider late submissions. Vendors must submit technical and administrative questions to Lacey Lockard at lacey.n.lockard.civ@health.mil no later than 14 October 2026, 1400 Eastern Time. As appropriate, the Government may post responses to questions or otherwise provide clarifications to all potential vendors. Per the CSO terms, the Government is not liable for costs associated with preparing materials submitted in response to this AOI. Interested parties are strongly encouraged to review all attached documents in their entirety for complete information regarding this opportunity, including submission requirements and other specific instructions.

title: Continuation of the Exceptional Longevity Data Management and Coordinating Center (EL DMCC) (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

input.description_text: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to support the continued operation and expansion of the Exceptional Longevity Data Management and Coordinating Center (EL DMCC) through a single U24 cooperative agreement award. The NOFO will be open to all eligible applicants. Established in 2022, the EL DMCC serves as the central hub for NIA’s human longevity translational research portfolio, integrating data and activities across studies to maximize the value of deeply phenotyped cohorts and associated genomic and multi-omics datasets. The DMCC currently plays a critical role in enabling cross-cohort analyses, coordinating collaborative research, and advancing shared data resources. Core functions include data harmonization and integration; development and implementation of common data standards; provision of statistical, computational, and artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) infrastructure and tools; coordination of cross-project collaborations; and managing shared data systems, including data storage, access, and platform operations. The DMCC also develops and maintains the ELITE (Exceptional Longevity Translational Resources) Portal, which provides secure access to harmonized datasets, analytical tools, and cloud-based computational workspaces. The DMCC supports controlled access to EL data and use of these resources by the research community and maintains ongoing efforts to ensure the Portal is interoperable with the NIA Alzheimer’s Disease Knowledge Portal and other data resources of the National Institutes of Health, consistent with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data principles. Through the NOFO, the Coordinating Center will be expected to build on and expand these core functions by: Enhancing integration of increasingly large and diverse datasets across cohorts and species Expanding statistical, computational, and AI/ML capabilities and associated infrastructure Developing and refining methods and standards for multi-omics data harmonization and integrative analyses Coordinating and supporting collaborative research across NIA-funded projects Developing and disseminating translational resources, including target nomination and prioritization resources, curated target knowledgebases, and inventories of candidate therapeutic targets Advancing the ELITE Portal, including improvements in data organization, search, visualization, interoperability, and cloud-based analytical environments Strengthening community engagement through training, workshops, and collaborative activities Applications are not being solicited at this time. This Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.

title: FEMA's Deployment Management Solution

input.description_text: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is conducting market research to identify commercial of the shelf (COTS), configurable commercial of the shelf (CCOTS), custom, or hybrid solutions capable of replacing the legacy Deployment Tracking System (DTS) and materially improving Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) incident workforce management capabilities. The replacement solution should support workforce readiness, personnel availability, qualifications, certifications, training, deployment tracking, incident and event staffing, force package management, equipment assignment, reporting, analytics, secure cloud hosting, and interoperability with existing FEMA and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) systems. FEMA is seeking information on solutions that improve readiness visibility, accelerate staffing, reduce manual work, strengthen data quality, support surge operations, improve reporting and analytics, and reduce long-term sustainment burden. The Government seeks commercial solutions that sustain reliable, secure, and continuously available legacy services while modernizing the platform toward scalable, cloud-native, API-driven, standards-based, and AI/ML-ready capabilities.
